# nish/host/text

Text in module storage, for a wasm module and the page that drives it (`docs/wp50-wasm-host.md` §7).

```ts
import {
  textRead,
  textWrite,
  textWriteF64,
  textWriteInt,
} from "nish/host/text";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { textRead, textWrite, textWriteInt } from "nish/host/text";

export const INBOX = new Array<u8>(256);
export const OUTBOX = new Array<u8>(256);

// The page: n = new TextEncoder().encodeInto(text, views.INBOX).written
export function echo(n: i32): i32 {
  const text = textRead(INBOX, n);
  if (text === null) return -1;
  return textWriteInt(OUTBOX, textWrite(OUTBOX, 0, text), toI64(n));
}
// The page: new TextDecoder().decode(views.OUTBOX.subarray(0, count))
```

</scalar-code-group>

</scalar-card>

</scalar-card>

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

A string crosses out of a module as an export's result or a host import's
argument, but an export cannot take one: the page writes text into a `u8[]`
the module declares as module storage and passes the byte count. These are
the module's halves of both directions:

</scalar-callout>

A writer takes the offset to write at and returns the offset after what it
wrote, so writes chain. Text that does not fit writes nothing and returns
-1, and every writer passes a -1 offset straight through, so a chain that
overflowed anywhere ends in -1 with the bytes before the failed write left
as they were. Nothing here traps on what a page wrote.

## Functions

### textRead

The first `n` bytes of `buf` as a string: what a page's `encodeInto` wrote.
The bytes are not checked as UTF-8; a sequence that is not becomes U+FFFD
when the string next crosses to the page.

```ts
function textRead(
  buf: readonly u8[],
  n: i32,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="buf" type="readonly u8[]" required>

the text's storage

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="n" type="i32" required>

the byte count the page passed

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

the string, or null when `n` is negative or past the buffer

</scalar-field>

### textWrite

Writes `s` as its UTF-8 bytes at offset `at`, or nothing when it does not fit.

```ts
function textWrite(
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  s: string,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

the text's storage

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

the offset to write at; a negative one is an earlier failure

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

the text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

the offset after the text, or -1 when `at` is negative or past the
  buffer, or the text does not fit

</scalar-field>

### textWriteF64

Writes `x` in its shortest round-tripping form, as a template literal
formats it: `0.30000000000000004`, `1e+21`, `NaN`, `-Infinity`.

```ts
function textWriteF64(
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  x: f64,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

the text's storage

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

the offset to write at; a negative one is an earlier failure

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="x" type="f64" required>

the number

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

the offset after the text, or -1 as `textWrite` answers it

</scalar-field>

### textWriteInt

Writes `n` in decimal, as a template literal formats it.

```ts
function textWriteInt(
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  n: i64,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

the text's storage

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

the offset to write at; a negative one is an earlier failure

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="n" type="i64" required>

the integer

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

the offset after the digits, or -1 as `textWrite` answers it

</scalar-field>
